$comment: Targets a fresh browser starts with. This file is the deployment's seeded
set: edit it, commit, redeploy, and any browser with an empty registry
picks it up. It does NOT overwrite a registry that already has targets --
Settings -> Restore starter targets does that, deliberately and on demand.
Adding a target in the running interface only writes to that browser's
registry. Nagios never sees it until the generated objects/ files are
exported, committed and redeployed -- until then the target stays Pending
because Nagios has no host or service by that name to report on.
address is a bare hostname or IP. Never include a scheme: Nagios passes
this straight to the check plugin as -H, and 'http://host' is not a
hostname, so the check fails with 'Invalid hostname, address or socket'.
check: ping | tcp | http | dns   (tcp needs port; http uses port/path/secure)
